main_topics.reason: The user described severe nausea after each weekly dose and repeatedly sought ways to manage it without stopping treatment.
The user first asked whether to quit and later checked whether to keep taking methotrexate until the appointment.
The user asked whether taking folic acid on methotrexate day was a problem and decided to move it to Sunday.
The user asked whether injections could reduce nausea and said they were scared of self-injecting, then considered trying other options first.
The user asked whether an anti-nausea medicine could be taken with methotrexate after learning it might be an option.
The user said methotrexate was helping their joints and hands, which informed their wish to avoid stopping it.
The user said they had thought the only options were to suffer or quit, and later reported feeling much better after hearing alternatives.
The user asked what to say at the appointment and agreed to write down the suggested questions.

output.summary: The user described severe weekend nausea after weekly methotrexate and wondered whether to stop, despite the medicine helping their hands. The assistant outlined options to discuss with the rheumatologist, including folic acid timing, dose-splitting, anti-nausea medicine, and injections; the user felt reassured, planned to move folic acid to Sunday, and agreed to keep taking methotrexate as prescribed until the appointment in about two weeks. The user said the conversation helped and planned to bring the assistant's suggested questions to the doctor.
